note: Manually curated ground truth for C1 Task 5. The gold `OTHER` label CANNOT be used as the evaluation target: of 78 OTHER tokens (after the Section D exclusions of R0017/R0008), only 9 are genuinely Tamil. 58 are purely numeric and 11 are identifiers or English ordinals -- annotation drift, documented in Section D.3. Evaluating a Tamil detector against raw OTHER would score it against a class that is 88% not-Tamil.
other_label_semantics: Per project owner: OTHER denotes Tamil specifically, because Tamil is a national language of Sri Lanka alongside Sinhala. It is not a generic not-SI-and-not-EN bucket, even though the annotations currently use it that way.

batch_2_note: Entries from R0049 onward were added after the October 2026 data batch (R0029-R0065). Only 1 of the 5 usable new entries is labelled OTHER in gold; the rest are labelled SI, so gold OTHER now misses much of the Tamil as well as being mostly numerals. Tamil in recordings excluded from C1 (corpus.EXCLUDED_RECORDINGS) is kept separately under tamil_in_excluded_recordings and is not scored, so positives and negatives come from the same recordings. Common Sinhala words that collide with Tamil lexicon entries (nama, nan, ne, enna, anna) were checked in context and are Sinhala.

tamil_sentence_in_sinhala_script.english: this is not a big problem
tamil_sentence_in_sinhala_script.why_it_matters: Five of the nine genuinely-Tamil tokens are this one sentence. The dominant form of Tamil in this corpus is Tamil written in SINHALA script, not romanized Tamil and not Tamil script. The implementation plan's Task 5 addresses only romanized Tamil and assumes a Unicode Tamil rule handles the rest; neither applies here.
